宏福苑「特設銷售計劃」踏入第三日（2日）揀樓，過去幾日揀樓期間，都有宏福苑業主反映「是迫於無奈」買樓，希望政府能豁免或寬減印花稅。《集誌社》整合特設銷售計劃網站上的單位資料，以及房委會、房協相關單位的從價印花稅列表，發現頭三日揀樓已售或已選的 99 個單位中，業主合共須繳付逾 700 萬元印花稅，當中 40 戶須繳付 10 萬元或以上。另外，房屋局局長何永賢今日在社交平台表示，截至 9 月 30 日，90.4% 宏福苑業主已完成簽署《買賣協議》。

The "Special Sales Scheme" website shows that 99 units have been selected or sold so far. (File photo)

The Housing Bureau previously stated that stamp duty is collected by the Stamp Office under the Inland Revenue Department, with rates ranging from HK$100 to a maximum of 6.5%, depending on the price or value of the property. Even for subsidised sale units sold below market value, the stamp duty is calculated based on the market value assessed by the Rating and Valuation Department, rather than the unit's original market value or sale price.

According to data as of the evening of 2 October, after the first three days of flat selection, the 99 units that have been selected or sold involve a total ad valorem stamp duty of over HK$7 million. Among them, 16 households need to pay more than HK$120,000 in stamp duty, while another 24 households need to pay between HK$100,000 and HK$120,000.

Of the 4,447 units across the 10 projects in the scheme, 1,288 have valuations exceeding HK$4 million, and owners are required to pay stamp duty of 2.5% of the price. (File photo)

Elderly owners have to top up HK$550,000 to "buy a flat"; stamp duty accounts for 15%

Taking Mrs. Tam, who is nearly 80 years old and selected a flat on the first day of selection, as an example, she chose a 482 sq ft unit at Hong Kong Housing Society's Fanling Lok Ling Hin on that day, priced at nearly HK$4.21 million. According to the HKHS stamp duty list, the market value of the unit assessed by the Rating and Valuation Department in August 2026 is HK$4.65 million, and the owner is required to pay HK$82,500 in stamp duty. Mrs. Tam and her 87-year-old husband have been struggling with the difficulty of renting a unit at their age. Although they have purchased their desired unit, after factoring in the government's acquisition price of approximately HK$3.74 million, and excluding legal fees, moving costs and furniture expenses, they have to top up HK$470,000 just for the property price alone, and together with stamp duty, the total subsidy is HK$550,000, with stamp duty alone accounting for nearly 15% of the overall cost.

10 projects, 4,447 units; nearly 30% subject to 2.5% ad valorem stamp duty

A review of the data shows that among the 4,447 units across the 10 projects offered under the Special Sales Scheme, only 420 units in total at Kam Tin Wui Hei Yuen, Tung Chung Yu Fung Court and Ping Shan Long Fung Court have valuations not exceeding HK$4 million, and owners only need to pay HK$100 in stamp duty to purchase these units. As for the remaining 7 projects with 4,027 units in total, 1,288 units (about 32%) have valuations exceeding HK$4 million, and owners are required to pay stamp duty of 2.5% of the price.

Among them, Kwun Tong Anderson Road Ho Yin provides 596 units, with 90% of units subject to the 2.5% stamp duty, of which 439 units are required to pay more than HK$55,000, and 45 of them have to pay about HK$120,000 to HK$130,000 in tax. The currently more popular Kai Tak Kai Yeung Court among Wang Fuk Court owners has half of its units (376) subject to ad valorem stamp duty, of which 208 are required to pay more than HK$55,000; Lok Ling Hin, another project more popular among owners, has 74% of its units (222) subject to ad valorem stamp duty, of which 194 are required to pay more than HK$55,000.

Secretary for Housing Winnie Ho stated on social media today that as of 30 September, 90.4% of Wang Fuk Court owners have completed signing the Agreement for Sale and Purchase; owners are required to complete signing the agreement on or before 15 October, and explanation teams will provide support during the flat selection process.
